text:
devon: quick dump of a weird perf regression I hit on Mistral-7B yesterday — saw 2.3x p50 token latency for long-context (2k) compared to baseline.
maya: ugh. did the kernel selector flip to a slower matmul path?
ravi: what workload? sampling or greedy?
devon: sampling, top-p 0.9, temperature 0.8. We were using speculative decoding with a Mixtral draft model (family pairing).
devon: pasted the perf-run command I used:

```
# perf harness
./run_infer --model=mistral-7b-q4_0 --max-len=2048 --sampler=top_p --p=0.9 --temp=0.8 --speculative_pair=mixtral-8b-draft --batch=16 --kv-cache=shared
```

maya: interesting — batch=16 + shared KV can cause cache thrash if draft pairing clips tokens or tokenizers mismatch. any traces?
devon: attached a short flame output: p50 310ms -> 720ms. CPU spin in kernel-select and kv-lookup.

ravi: can you paste the kernel selection logs? our selector prints reason codes now.
devon: here you go:

```
[2026-02-10T14:12:01Z] kernel_selector: model=mistral-7b arch=attn-rotary rope_scale=1.0 heads=32 kv_dim=64
[2026-02-10T14:12:01Z] kernel_selector: selected=matmul_fused_32bit reason=precision_prop latency_est=8.2us
[2026-02-10T14:12:01Z] kernel_selector: fallback_to=matmul_split reason=kv_cache_mismatch
```

maya: fallback_to=matmul_split + kv_cache_mismatch — that's the smoking gun.
lena: why kv_cache_mismatch though? model dims look consistent. Is the draft model generating different tokenization lengths causing alignment issues?
opsay: infra-bot detected out-of-band tokenizer ID between pair: mistral-7b (tokenizer v3) vs mixtral-8b-draft (tokenizer v2). Flagging mismatch.

ravi: tokenizer mismatch would cause the draft acceptance rate to plummet, forcing many speculative rollbacks and KV invalidations. acceptance rate stats?
devon: acceptance rate dropped to 18% (normally ~62%). See quick stat dump: 

```
speculative: attempts=1250 accept=225 accept_rate=0.18 avg_latency_with_draft=260ms avg_latency_without_draft=430ms
kv_invalidations=430 kv_invalidation_rate=0.34
```

maya: so the draft is often rejected, but it still writes KV or causes pathing that triggers the runtime to invalidate caller-side caches.
lena: also look at RoPE scaling: Mistral was using rope_scale=1.0, Mixtral draft had rope_scale=0.95 in metadata. That can lead to attention score drift and different generation boundaries.

ravi: twofold fix path: 1) reject draft pairing if tokenizer_id or rope_scale mismatch, 2) make KV cache updates transactional so rejected drafts don't cause global invalidation.

devon: transactional KV update sounds heavier. can we at least make the selector avoid matmul_split by aligning kernels when mismatch is only tokenizer?

maya: kernel selection obeys compatibility matrix: if model metadata mismatch, it errs on the side of safety and falls back. We can add a finer-grained codepath: allow speculative drafts to use isolating KV segments that are merged on accept. cheaper than full transactional commit.

opsay: infra-bot: created ticket INF-4827 "speculative: isolate KV writes for draft pairing" assigned to eng-runtime.

lena: also want to tune acceptance threshold — we saw low acceptance due to tokenizer mapping differences. Could we normalize token mappings (fallback mapping table) between paired families to boost acceptance from 18% -> ~50%?
ravi: maybe, but mapping risks semantic drift. Better: enforce exact tokenizer compatibility for auto-pairing and allow manual override with explicit opt-in.

devon: for immediate mitigation I rolled out a hotfix to disable draft pairing for Mistral -> Mixtral combos in prod yesterday. p50 recovered to 340ms.

maya: good stopgap. For next steps:
- add metadata checks during pairing (tokenizer_id, rope_scale, kv_dim, head_count)
- introduce isolated-kv draft mode (fast-path)
- add telemetry: draft_accept_rate, kv_invalidation_per_pairing, kernel_fallback_counts
- small doc in runtimes about safe pairing rules

ravi: I'll own the metadata check PR. estimated 2d. lena you take isolation prototype?
lena: will prototype isolated KV segments, should be 3d.

devon: one more observation — RoPE scaling mismatch caused higher per-token attention variance which increased sampling entropy and made top-p unstable. worth adding a validation test that runs a small prompt and compares ngram overlap between candidate pair models.

opsay: infra-bot: linked logs https://logs.internal/redwood/1765551234 for owners devon,ravi,lena.

maya: nice. leave a note for release engineers: disabling pairings changes load patterns (more direct calls to Mistral) — may need to tweak autoscaler thresholds for Mistral pools.
ravi: noted. will update autoscale config once PR merges.

devon: thanks all. I'll follow up with perf traces and a minimal repro snippet.

lena: thanks — sounds actionable. :thumbsup:
